Making slides in the GDS template is easy, and going from a set of notes to a finished deck is much faster than building it by hand.

Give Claude your notes. It agrees the headings, then builds the deck.

OFFICIAL

Set it up once

1

Install it

From govuk-once/gds-claude-plugins, with two commands.

2

Or use a repo

Some repos already include it, such as personalised-planning.

3

Run the check

Ask Claude to run the gds-slides setup check.

5

Numbered cards, for steps or requirements. Install with /plugin marketplace add govuk-once/gds-claude-plugins, then /plugin install gds-slides@gds-claude-plugins. The setup check reports anything missing and how to fix it. Python 3 is enough for HTML decks; PowerPoint needs python-pptx, photos need Pillow, and previews need DeckCraft.

OFFICIAL

Ask for a deck in plain words

“Make a GDS deck for Thursday's show and tell on what we learnt from the beta. Here are my notes and some photos.”

6

Say who the deck is for if you can, point Claude at the documents it should draw on, and give it any photos or screenshots you want in the deck.

OFFICIAL

Five steps from brief to deck

Claude agrees the headings with you before it writes the outline, so changing the story costs nothing.

7

Brief: who the deck is for and the one thing they should take away. Headings: for you to approve. Outline: a Markdown file you can read and edit, a heading per slide, with detail in the speaker notes. Build: both formats at once. Look: Claude checks every slide and fixes the outline until they all pass.

OFFICIAL

Pick the slide for the point

Ask forYou get
A sentence or a short listA text slide, like the last one
A comparisonA table, ruled like this one
One line said largeA quote, with who said it
A flow or a modelA diagram, drawn in the GDS style
A photo or a screenshotAn image slide, or a photo behind a section
8

A table slide. Ask in plain words, for example: make slide 4 a table comparing the two options.

OFFICIAL

Break a point into parts

Cards suit a few things that sit side by side.

Cards

Two to four panels, each a title and a sentence or list.

A muted line holds the figure or source.

Numbered cards

The same panels, numbered, for steps or requirements.

Scorecards

A table where cells say yes, partly or no, with a short note.

A callout holds the takeaway the reader must not miss. One a slide at most.
9

A cards slide with a lede, an evidence line and a callout. For a deck people will read on screens rather than watch, add Density: discuss under the title for smaller type and more words a slide.

OFFICIAL

Make a document instead of a slide deck if you are trying to say too much.

The GDS slide template
10

A quote slide, for a callout or something a user said. Keep it to one or two lines.

OFFICIAL

One outline. Two formats.

11

Text over an image: a photo section slide, with your own photo under the navy tint. Leave the image line out to use the template's photo. Use it at most once a deck.

OFFICIAL

One outline, both versions

One command builds both files from the outline.

12

A diagram slide. Both files land in decks/<name>/, beside the outline. Diagrams are drawn as SVG by a short script kept with the deck. Diagram and split slides also take a PNG or JPEG, for screenshots.

OFFICIAL

Each format does its own job

Work on the PowerPoint file. Show the HTML file.

What you needPowerPointHTML
Edit in fine detail● Yes○ No
Comment together● Yesin PowerPoint for the web○ No
Share as one file◐ Partlyneeds Office● Yesany browser
Present with notes● Yes● YesP presents, N for notes
13

A scorecard table. Share the PowerPoint file when people need to edit or comment, in PowerPoint for the web. Send the HTML file when they only need to read or present it: P presents, N shows speaker notes, arrow keys move.

OFFICIAL
14

A photo slide: two or three photos on the template's cyan frame, or navy with {navy} after the heading. The heading isn't shown; it names the slide for screen readers and the notes. Photos are cropped from the centre to fill their frame.

OFFICIAL

To change a deck, change the outline

Ask Claude to edit the outline, or edit it yourself, then rebuild. Both formats stay the same.

Changed it in PowerPoint? Claude edits that file in place instead, so your changes stay.
15

The outline is the master copy until someone edits the PowerPoint file by hand. From then on Claude changes the PowerPoint file itself: wording, speaker notes, hiding and reordering slides, and it checks the result against a backup slide by slide.

OFFICIAL

Good to know

  • OFFICIAL material only
  • Open an important deck in PowerPoint first
  • Photos are cropped to fill their frame
  • Diagrams reach PowerPoint as pictures
16

Every slide is marked OFFICIAL. PowerPoint can wrap text slightly differently from the HTML deck. Crop a photo yourself first if its subject is near the edge. To change a diagram, change its SVG and rebuild.
